subject.title: Slack: Show tool-level progress in assistant thread status

question: Should OpenClaw add native Slack assistant-thread status updates for active tool progress, and if so what visibility/default and write cadence should it use?
rationale: Current source makes the feature gap clear, but choosing tool-detail visibility in shared Slack threads is a product/security decision that should align with the open Slack-safe progress visibility work.

options.title: Approve gated native status work
options.body: Implement per-tool assistant-thread status only after choosing a safe/default visibility policy, deduplicating repeated labels, and requiring live Slack proof of transitions and clearing.

options.title: Rely on current progress surfaces
options.body: Keep fixed rotating loading messages plus draft/status-reaction progress as the supported Slack UX and close or narrow native per-tool status work later.

options.title: Fold into broader Slack visibility policy
options.body: Track any native status label implementation under the Slack-safe progress visibility decision so all Slack progress surfaces share one disclosure model.

recommendation.title: Approve gated native status work
recommendation.body: Implement per-tool assistant-thread status only after choosing a safe/default visibility policy, deduplicating repeated labels, and requiring live Slack proof of transitions and clearing.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent merged work and follow-up commits show the strongest current ownership signal for Slack assistant status behavior and adjacent UX decisions.
